title: RF wireless component
description: One wireless transmitter/receiver system, normalised from Research/Wireless Microphone_RF_Components.json. That source is nested Manufacturer -> Model -> Range; this schema keeps the same grain by making the model the record and its tuning ranges an ordered list, because a range is a variant of a system rather than a product of its own. Deliberately NOT the microphone schema: an RF system has no capsule, polar pattern or transducer, and a microphone has no tuning range or preset count.

source.description: Where the record came from, and the keys it is addressed by.

manufacturer_key.description: Verbatim top-level key in the source, e.g. 'Audio Technica'.

brand_slug.description: Brand this is filed under in the browser. Reuses the microphone brand slug when the manufacturer already sells mics (EV -> Electro-Voice), so wireless gear intermixes with that vendor's catalogue.

model_slug.description: URL-safe id within the brand. Always prefixed 'rf-' so it can never collide with a microphone model slug.

manufacturer.description: Display name, taken from the microphone brand when one matched.

kind.description: Distinguishes these records from microphones wherever the two share a list.

component_type.description: Always 'wireless-system' for this dataset; present so other RF component classes (antennas, distros) can join later.

bands.description: Distinct VHF/UHF markers across the model's ranges. Nearly always a single value; a model spanning both keeps both.

subtitle.description: Generated one-liner, e.g. 'UHF wireless system · 6 tuning ranges · 480–820 MHz'.

coverage.description: Envelope across every range the model offers. Ranges are usually disjoint, so span_mhz is the outer envelope, not the sum of tunable width.

tunable_mhz.description: Sum of the individual range widths.

name.description: The range's own 'range' field; usually equal to key.

presets.description: num_presets: how many prebuilt frequencies the range carries.

setting.description: A coordination setting that is either a spacing in MHz or one of the source's tokens. Both forms are kept: `mhz` is null unless the source gave a number, and `mode` always says which it was.
